terms.gloss: an inch: a twelfth of a foot
terms.comment: A twelfth of anything: of an inheritance, of a pound (an ounce), and of the foot (pēs), which makes it the Roman inch. It also means a scrap, a bit: nūlla uncia, not a scrap (Mart. 9.49.12).

evidence: M-O s.v. US length: inch (Lüders 1826; Goelzer)
Caes. BG 3.13: clāvī digitī pollicis crassitūdine (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically the thumb; Cato and Caesar use the thumb’s breadth as a rough measure of thickness, and modern Latin made it the inch. digitus, a finger’s breadth, is the sixteenth of a foot; Lewis & Short calls it an inch too (Caes. BG 7.73.6).

phrases.latin: Hic clāvus vix unciam longus est.
phrases.english: This nail is barely an inch long.

sources: Lewis & Short: uncia · Lewis & Short: pollex
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. US length: inch.
